name: Subsea production systems (trees, manifolds, umbilicals)
principle: Wells are completed on the seabed with trees, linked by manifolds, jumpers, umbilicals and flowlines to a host. TechnipFMC delivered its 100th standardised Subsea 2.0 tree in May 2025 with lead times about a third shorter than engineered-to-order trees; Westwood counted 255 tree awards in 2024.

source.note: Westwood Energy, Global Subsea Tree Tracker 2025

performance.metric: world water-depth records for subsea completions (Gulf of Mexico Perdido development)
performance.unit: m water depth (Silvertip 9,356 ft = 2,851 m record Dec 2008; Tobago about 2,925 m world's deepest subsea completion)
performance.basis: Shell set a world water-depth record completing a subsea well 9,356 ft below sea level at Silvertip (OGJ, 3 Dec 2008); Tobago, in roughly 2,925 m of water, is the world's deepest subsea completion (Offshore Magazine, 1 Dec 2010); tieback-distance records not found in this pass

source.note: Offshore Magazine, 1 Dec 2010 (read 2026-10-28); OGJ 3 Dec 2008 for the Silvertip 9,356 ft record

advantages: Standardisation shortens time to first oil
limitations: Equipment details (depth ratings, tieback limits) are not on the pages read

sources.note: Westwood Energy, Global Subsea Tree Tracker 2025
Oil & Gas Journal, Shell sets record with Perdido well completion, 3 Dec 2008
